A retroactive tail sampler. Every span is buffered to disk for a retention
window `W`; when a keep signal arrives — an error, a latency threshold, a
baggage-carried timing, a user OTTL policy, or the deterministic baseline —
the trace's buffered spans are flushed to the rest of the pipeline, however
long ago they arrived within `W`. Spans never kept simply age out. There is
no pass-through mode: a batch is either buffered or refused with a retryable
error.

The processor is built for 24/7 line-rate operation: the ingest path
performs zero bookkeeping allocations per span, buffering is
marshal-on-ingest to disk segments (not retained pdata), and a blocked
exporter never blocks ingest.

## How it works

- **Buffer**: spans are fragmented and appended to per-shard disk segments;
  a compact index (~150 B per live trace) maps trace ids to fragments.
  Fragments survive restart; expiry is by whole segment at `W`.
- **Decide**: keep detection runs at ingest — `keep_on_error`, span/trace
  latency thresholds, trace age via baggage timing, OTTL policies, and a
  deterministic baseline rate (identical verdict on every instance by
  construction, never broadcast). Decisions are recorded in a decided set
  and are exactly-once: duplicates are absorbed, never re-flushed.
- **Broadcast**: in a multi-instance deployment each locally decided keep is
  published on a bus so peers flush their fragments of the same trace. NATS
  is the supported backend (core pub/sub or JetStream durable with a ≤`W`
  replay horizon). With no bus configured, an in-process loopback runs the
  full decide→flush loop single-instance with no infrastructure.
- **Degrade explicitly**: a disk watermark early-expires the oldest
  segments, never past a configurable window floor; at the floor (and on a
  full shard queue) the processor refuses batches with a retryable error.
  Every shed and refusal is counted — there are no silent drops.

## Getting started

Minimal single-instance configuration (`storage_dir` and `disk_budget` are
required — a retroactive sampler that cannot buffer cannot sample):

```yaml
processors:
  retrosampler:
    storage_dir: /var/lib/otelcol/retrosampler
    disk_budget: 42949672960 # bytes the buffer may occupy on disk
    window: 5m
    keep_on_error: true
```

Multi-instance, with keeps broadcast over JetStream:

```yaml
processors:
  retrosampler:
    storage_dir: /var/lib/otelcol/retrosampler
    disk_budget: 42949672960
    window: 5m # every instance in the fleet must share one window
    bus:
      type: nats
      nats:
        url: nats://nats:4222
        mode: durable # or at_most_once (core pub/sub, counted loss)
```

## Configuration

| Field | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `storage_dir` | (required) | Root of the disk buffer. |
| `disk_budget` | (required) | Bytes the buffer may occupy across shards. |
| `window` | `5m` | Retention window `W`. |
| `window_floor` | `1m` | Minimum effective window the watermark may shrink to; below it, backpressure. |
| `watermark_pct` | `80` | Percent of `disk_budget` above which oldest segments expire early. |
| `shards` | `GOMAXPROCS` | Single-writer worker count, capped at `GOMAXPROCS`. |
| `segment_size` | `32MiB` | Per-shard segment roll threshold in bytes. |
| `keep_on_error` | `true` | Keep traces containing an error-status span. |
| `span_latency_threshold` | off | Keep when any span's duration reaches the threshold. |
| `trace_latency_threshold` | off | Keep on baggage-carried `elapsed_ms` reaching the threshold. |
| `trace_age_threshold` | off | Keep on `now − T0` (baggage-carried trace start) reaching the threshold. |
| `baseline_rate` | `0` | Deterministic sample of \[0,1]; identical verdict on every instance, local-only. |
| `policies` | `[]` | `{name, condition}` list of OTTL span conditions, first match wins. |
| `t0_attribute` | `baggage.t0` | Span attribute carrying the trace-start epoch millis. |
| `elapsed_ms_attribute` | `baggage.elapsed_ms` | Span attribute carrying elapsed millis. |
| `bus` | none (in-process) | `type: nats` plus a `nats` block: `url` (required), `mode` (`durable` default / `at_most_once`), `subject` (`retrosampler.keeps`), `stream` (`retrosampler-keeps`), `creds_file`. |

## Delivery semantics

Decisions are exactly-once; span delivery is at-least-once. Batch retries
after a refusal, flush retries after a downstream failure, and durable-bus
replay after a restart can each duplicate spans — deduplication belongs to
the backend, as elsewhere in OpenTelemetry pipelines. Two bounded loss
windows are accepted and monitored rather than closed: a locally detected
keep is lost if the instance dies before publishing it (watch
`published.keeps` against `kept.local`), and an exporter outage longer than
`W` loses fragments to expiry (counted).

## Telemetry

The processor exports its instruments under
`otelcol.processor.retrosampler.*`; see [documentation.md](documentation.md)
for the generated reference. The signals worth alerting on first:
`pending.flushes` growing without draining, any
`pending.publishes_abandoned`, any `bus.errors`, a widening
`kept.local` − `published.keeps` gap, `flush.age.ratio` mass near 1.0
(window too tight), and the `shed.floor_protected` /
`shed.nothing_reclaimable` counters (the disk ladder out of room).

## Deployment notes

Keep `memory_limiter` first in the pipeline; set `GOMEMLIMIT` to ~90% of
the container limit. Size `disk_budget` to hold `W ×` ingest rate with
headroom above the watermark. Decided-set memory sizes at roughly 64 B ×
fleet-wide keep rate × `W`. A fleet must share one `window`; a mixed-`W`
fleet is a configuration error.

## Development

Architecture decisions live in [docs/adrs](docs/adrs/README.md); the
performance budgets (zero-alloc ingest, testbed floors) are enforced as
tests. `make test` runs the race suite, `make generate` regenerates from
`metadata.yaml`, `make build` produces an ocb collector, `make testbed`
runs the load validation. Licensed under [Apache-2.0](LICENSE).
